summary.headline: Talbros Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR241 crore with record 18.7% EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 15-20% growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter by its account, with consolidated revenue of INR241 crore (up from INR211 crore) and EBITDA of INR45 crore at an 18.7% margin. FY26 revenue was INR1,383 crore (up 5%), EBITDA INR155 crore (17.5% margin) and PAT INR104 crore (up 10%). Management said the company is moving from order acquisition to execution, with several delayed orders (Stellantis, a European EV customer, Forging, Cummins, JLR) now starting in FY27. Forging margins were pressured in Q4 by pass-through of raw material and rupee-driven price resets.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY; one answer cited 16-20%.
Management targets crossing INR1,000 crore revenue in FY27 (said to be 'definitely' targeted).
EBITDA margin guided at 17-18% for FY27 (one answer said 17% definitely).
Marelli Talbros FY27 revenue growth guided at 35-40%; Talbros Marugo around 15%.
Q1 FY27 top-line expected to be broadly similar to Q4 FY26; H2 expected to be significantly better than H1.
Forging margins expected to normalise within one or two quarters; management asked investors to focus on full-year margins rather than quarterly.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex planned at INR31 crore, with about INR103 crore planned for FY27 (per prepared remarks); FY27 split to be finalised at end of Q3 FY27.
FY26 capex for Gasket & Heat Shield about INR16 crore (new business, including expected Cummins USA business); asset turnover above 3x.
Forging capex of INR60 crore for FY26 (Marelli business INR90 crore plus DANA, GKN); INR45-47 crore for plant and equipment, rest for infrastructure.
Marelli capex about INR20 crore for European customer machines; Marugo capex about INR7 crore. About 25% of the total capex already spent; to complete by September-October 2026.
Marelli Gujarat facility capex shifted from FY26 to FY27-28 following Maruti and Tata orders; site search to start in Q3 and plant online next year.
demand_pricing: Industry: PV Q4 sales record 13.16 lakh units (+13% YoY); two-wheelers 57.73 lakh units (+26%); CV 3.25 lakh units (record); EV cars about +50% and EV two-wheelers about +39% YoY.

Order book: management says about 70% of the order book will be commercialised by end of FY26; Stellantis INR1,000 crore chassis order (about INR150 crore per year over 5 years) to start June 2026, with INR100 crore expected in FY27.

Delayed orders now starting: European EV order from September; Korean customer Heat Shield order (about INR20 crore per year) started; Forging INR500 crore order from October; Kia first order started February; Cummins first billing June; JLR billing from September.

Pricing: raw material and exchange-rate price changes passed through to customers with a lag of one to three months; Forging price resets delayed in Q4 by one to two months, and management says 60-70% of the benefit from earlier months was passed to customers.

Competition: management cites China-plus-one sourcing and single-source wins; one vendor-bankruptcy example where Talbros supplied at 15-20% lower price to a major OEM. Exports expected to rise to about 30% of revenue in one to two years (about one-fourth in FY26).

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth since FY24 lagged the order wins of about INR4,000 crore, and were there internal factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delays were largely customer-driven: a European EV order was delayed (now 50/50 EV mix, starting September), the Stellantis order starts June, and Forging orders slipped a year. Earlier 5-year order books of INR326 crore and INR431 crore delivered only partly in annual revenue terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the standalone business grow double digits in FY27, and what is the margin outlook given input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, double-digit growth expected; at least INR60-70 crore of new billing from new part numbers. Management asked investors not to focus on quarterly margins, saying price increases are generally recovered in one to three months through proprietary products and metal/exchange-linked pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned by division and what is the outlook for the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex of INR16 crore in Gasket and Heat Shield, INR60 crore in Forging, about INR20 crore Marelli, and about INR7 crore Marugo. FY27 capex to be worked out at end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18-20% aspirational growth purely organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management referred to consolidated revenue of INR1,383 crore; new business of INR150-160 crore commercialising in June and October adds about 11-12%, with the balance from 6-7% market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Forging margin compressed in Q4 with revenue up 11% and EBITDA up only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a delayed price decrease pass-through in July-August and a price reset on 1 January after rupee depreciation; the benefit was passed on partly to customers. Margins expected to recover in one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Maruti at about 20% of revenue a concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers have 60-65% customer dependence, so 20% is comfortable; the share reflects strong passenger vehicle growth and high content per vehicle across all divisions except forgings. Exports expected to reach 30% in one to two years.

risks_watch: Execution on delayed orders (Stellantis from June, European EV from September, JLR billing from September, Forging from October); repeated delays in past years.
Margin pressure from raw material and freight costs linked to West Asia tensions, and lagged price pass-through.
Customer concentration: Maruti about 20% of top-10 revenue and about 90% of Marugo revenue.
Rupee depreciation and price-reset timing affecting Forging margins.
Gujarat plant of Marelli deferred to FY27-28; FY27 capex to be confirmed at Q3.
Management has not disclosed the new CEO's KPIs; a five-year outlook is expected before Diwali.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, order wins and FY27 growth, while candid about Forging margin pressure and delayed order timelines. Several answers were reassuring but gave few hard numbers on FY27 capex and total order book.
key_quotes: We remain confident of delivering a 15% to 20% year-on-year growth in '27.
Our focus will be to maintain EBITDA margins between 17% to 18% through product mix and operational leverage as well as cost management.

I just want request investors, don't look at quarterly margins. Wait for the year, because when we launch the prices increase, we have launched with the customers, sometimes it takes one month, sometimes three months to settle.
As you all know, there are inflationary pressures that are coming our way, but we have to manage that, and we'll try and pass on the cost to the customers.
The company is now moving from a phase of order acquisition to execution.
